This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. Michigan Republican Senate candidate
Mike Rogers released an ad today calling for an end to President Trump's trade war with
Canada. Here in Michigan, we know that Canada is not our enemy. We need to end this tariff
war now. Rogers had previously defended some of Trump's tariffs as necessary. It's the
second time Rogers has split with Trump recently after calling for an end to the Iran war,
which he previously supported. Asked about the ad today, Trump suggested Rogers wasn't
breaking with him on the issue, saying, "I viewed it as wanting Canada to make a deal."
Trump is heading to a campaign event in Texas later today. Today marks three years since
Hamas launched its surprise attack on Israel leading to the war in Gaza. As memorials are
being held across the country, many Israelis are grappling with new reports that Prime
Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was warned about an impending attack, as NPR's Kat Lonsdorf
reports.
Officials in both Egypt and the United Arab Emirates repeatedly warned Netanyahu about
a serious, looming attack by Hamas from Gaza in 2023. NPR has spoken to four people in the
Middle East with knowledge of those warnings. First reported by the Israeli newspaper Haaretz
as well as The Atlantic and The New York Times, the revelations are dominating conversations
in Israel, just weeks before national elections that will determine Netanyahu's political
future. Netanyahu has denied he was warned, calling the reports fake news and filing a
defamation lawsuit last week against the Israeli outlets that published them.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
A tropical storm is brewing in the Gulf of Mexico. NPR's Debbie Elliott reports its forecast
to strengthen into the first hurricane of the Atlantic hurricane season.
Tropical storm Isaias formed over the western Gulf overnight. The National Hurricane Center
says it's on track to rapidly gain strength as it moves to the east over warm Gulf waters
and could become a hurricane by Thursday. Forecasters say residents from Louisiana to
the Florida Gulf Coast should be prepared for damaging winds, heavy rain and dangerous
storm surge. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has declared a state of emergency in 25 counties
in the Panhandle and Big Bend region, freeing up resources to be staged for a hurricane
response. This year's hurricane season has been dampened by a strong El Niño weather
pattern which hinders Atlantic storm development. Debbie Elliott, NPR News.
Lawyers for a Texas man who fatally shot a convenience store clerk are asking a judge
to stay his execution by lethal injection, citing the recent failed execution of Christa
Pike in Tennessee. Attorneys for Jamal Howard say the same drug used in Pike's attempted
execution, Pentobarbital, would be used in Texas and they argue the state's supply could
be degraded. US stocks pulled back from their records today. The S&P 500 slipped nearly
a quarter of a percent a day after topping its prior all-time high. The Dow dropped more
than half a percent. This is NPR News.
The University of Arizona has suspended activities at its fraternities after reports of misconduct,
including assault and hazing. The school's dean of students says the reports involve
nearly half the school's intra-fraternity council chapters. Some cases are under criminal
investigation. The suspension follows the recent public outcry over how Cornell University
handled fraternity rape allegations in 2024.
This year's Nobel Prize in Chemistry has gone to two researchers for their work involving
a unique property of certain molecules, NPR's Ari Daniel reports.
Put one hand on top of the other. They look alike, but they're not identical. A molecule
with this property, where it can't be superimposed on its mirror image, is called chiral. Certain
key molecules of life are chiral, like amino acids and DNA. The Nobel committee recognized
two chemists for their separate experiments explaining and amplifying this molecular asymmetry,
with repercussions for drugs, flavors, and novel materials. Kenso Sohai, now professor
emeritus at Tokyo University of Science, is one of the recipients.
Of course, this is one of the most exciting days in my life.
A speaker at today's ceremony called Sohai's work, quote, "probably the coolest experiment
in organic chemistry." Ari Daniel, NPR News.
The University of Nevada, Las Vegas is set to graduate its first student with a minor
in mariachi. The program was launched to encourage students to become mariachi educators in the
Clark County School District, which has one of the largest mariachi programs in the country.
I'm Rylan Barton. You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
